title: Odd derivations on free graded divided-power polynomial algebras
statement: Let $S$ be a commutative ring and $P$ a nonnegative strictly graded commutative graded divided-power polynomial $S$-algebra, in the sense of the underlying graded algebra in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga], with a specified set $J_e$ of generators in each degree $e\geq0$, finite for each $e$. No differential is given on $P$. Given elements $v_j\in P_{e-1}$ for all generators $j\in J_e$, with $v_j=0$ when $e=0$, there is a unique $S$-linear map $\delta:P_i\to P_{i-1}$ satisfying $\delta(j)=v_j$, the signed rule $\delta(xy)=\delta(x)y+(-1)^{\deg(x)}x\delta(y)$ for homogeneous $x,y$, and $\delta(\gamma_n(x))=\delta(x)\gamma_{n-1}(x)$ for every positive even-degree homogeneous $x$ and $n\geq1$. No condition $\delta^2=0$ or $\delta(v_j)=0$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), proof, first paragraph: the existence of a lift satisfying (1),(2), and the hint to proceed one variable at a time. This is the generatorwise odd-operator construction underlying that hint, without the square-zero constraint on a differential.

proof.text: Use the polynomial model in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga]: $P$ arises from $P_0=S[J_0]$ by successive adjunctions of sets of variables of one positive degree, in a sequence not necessarily ordered by degree. Fix an ordering of each finite $J_e$, $e>0$, and let $P'$ arise from $S[J_0]$ by adjoining the generators one at a time in these orders by increasing degree; by clauses (3),(4) of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] this is the set adjunction degree by degree followed by the union. Iterating the free module decompositions of clauses (1)--(4), $P$ and $P'$ are free $S[J_0]$-modules on standard monomials: products of distinct generators, an odd generator with exponent $0$ or $1$, a positive even generator $T$ as $T^{[m]}$, $m\geq0$, factors in the respective adjunction order. Send a standard monomial of $P'$ to the product in $P$ of the same factors and extend $S[J_0]$-linearly. Reordering factors changes only a sign, so this is a graded isomorphism $\phi:P'\to P$. It is multiplicative, since in both algebras products of standard monomials reduce by the same rules: strict graded commutativity, $T^2=0$ for odd $T$, and $T^{[a]}T^{[b]}=\binom{a+b}{a}T^{[a+b]}$ with $T^{[a]}=\gamma_a(T)$. So $\phi$ fixes $S[J_0]$, every generator and every $T^{[a]}$. We construct the operator on $P'$ and transport it by $\phi$; steps 5--6 use only these values and the divided powers of $P$ itself. Every element uses finitely many generators. The subalgebra of $P'$ on $J_0$ and the generators of degree below $e$ contains $P'_{e-1}$, as degrees are nonnegative, so $v_T$ (read in $P'$ via $\phi$) is present when $T$ of degree $e$ is adjoined. Begin with the zero operator on $S[J_0]$.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), proof, omitted operator lift (1),(2), hint: proceed one variable at a time; explicit argument by the worker using Tags 09PH,09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even), 0F4I (remark-adjoining-set-of-variables), and 09PG (definition-divided-powers-graded).

proof.text: Suppose a degree $-1$ signed derivation $D_A$ has been constructed on the preceding subalgebra $A$. For the next generator $T$ of degree $e>0$, put $v=v_T\in A_{e-1}$. Use the free left $A$-module description of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] to define, for homogeneous $a\in A_p$, $D(aT^{[m]})=D_A(a)T^{[m]}+(-1)^p avT^{[m-1]}$ for $m\geq1$, and $D(a)=D_A(a)$. In odd degree only $m=1$ occurs and $T^{[1]}$ means $T$; in even degree all $m\geq1$ occur. Extend $S$-linearly using the unique normal forms. Both terms have degree $p+me-1$, and $D(T)=v$. This constructs a linear operator independently of any Leibniz or square-zero assertion.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), proof, omitted operator lift (1),(2), hint: proceed one variable at a time; explicit argument by the worker using Tags 09PH,09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even), 0F4I (remark-adjoining-set-of-variables), and 09PG (definition-divided-powers-graded).

proof.text: For even $e$, verify the signed Leibniz rule on $aT^{[m]},bT^{[n]}$, where $a\in A_p,b\in A_q$. By [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] their product is $\binom{m+n}{m}abT^{[m+n]}$. In differentiating, the $D_A(a),D_A(b)$ terms agree by the inductive Leibniz rule. Since $v$ has odd degree, move it past $b$ with sign $(-1)^q$, using [def-sfb-nonnegative-strict-graded-algebra]. The two remaining coefficients of $(-1)^{p+q}abvT^{[m+n-1]}$ on the Leibniz side are $\binom{m+n-1}{m-1}$ and $\binom{m+n-1}{m}$. Their sum is $\binom{m+n}{m}$ by Pascal's integer identity. If $m=0$ or $n=0$, omit the corresponding derivative term; if both vanish this is exactly the rule in $A$. Bilinearity proves the rule on all homogeneous inputs.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), proof, omitted operator lift (1),(2), hint: proceed one variable at a time; explicit argument by the worker using Tags 09PH,09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even), 0F4I (remark-adjoining-set-of-variables), and 09PG (definition-divided-powers-graded).

proof.text: For odd $e$, $v$ is even and commutes with $A$ and $T$. Check the four products of module types $a,b$ and $aT,bT$. The first type is the rule in $A$. The mixed types follow by expansion of $D(aT)=D_A(a)T+(-1)^p av$ and $Tb=(-1)^q bT$; in particular $D(Tb)=bv+(-1)^qD_A(b)T=v b-TD_A(b)$, as required. For the product of two $T$ terms the product is zero. Its Leibniz expression has its two terms not containing $T^2$ equal to $(-1)^p abvT$ and $(-1)^{p+1}abvT$, whose sum is zero; the other terms contain $T^2=0$. Here $p=\deg(a)$ and $q=\deg(b)$. These are precisely the multiplication and strict sign rules of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] and [def-sfb-nonnegative-strict-graded-algebra], so no division by $2$ is used.

source.place: Tag 09PS (lemma-get-derivation), proof, omitted operator lift (1),(2), hint: proceed one variable at a time; explicit argument by the worker using Tags 09PH,09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even), 0F4I (remark-adjoining-set-of-variables), and 09PG (definition-divided-powers-graded).

proof.text: Repeat steps 2--4 on $P'$ using the fixed orders of step 1, and let $P'^{(e)}$ be the algebra after all generators of degrees at most $e$ have been adjoined. Every extension restricts to the preceding operator, so their values agree on overlaps. Clause (4) of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] identifies $P'$ with the union of these completed degree stages; empty generator sets give identity inclusions. Define $\delta'$ there by its agreeing restrictions. Any two homogeneous elements and their product occur in a single stage; hence $\delta'$ is $S$-linear, of degree $-1$, and satisfies the signed Leibniz rule. Put $\delta=\phi\delta'\phi^{-1}$ on $P$. Since $\phi$ is an isomorphism of graded algebras fixing every generator, $\delta$ is $S$-linear of degree $-1$, satisfies the signed Leibniz rule and $\delta(j)=v_j$. For a positive even generator $T$, [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] gives $\gamma_m(T)=T^{[m]}=\phi(T^{[m]})$ in $P$, so $\delta(\gamma_m(T))=v_TT^{[m-1]}=\delta(T)\gamma_{m-1}(T)$ for every $m\geq1$ by the defining formula of step 2. All specified degree-zero generators have value zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-pd-derivation-compatibility-closure] to $(P,\delta)$ and write $C_\delta$ for its compatibility locus. Each positive even generator belongs to $C_\delta$ by step 5, so every $\gamma_m(T)$ belongs to it by closure under iterated divided powers. Every positive even-degree monomial with no odd generators is an even multiple of one such $\gamma_m(T)$ and therefore lies in $C_\delta$. A monomial with odd generators has an even positive number of them; factor off one odd generator and write it as $uv$ with both factors homogeneous odd, so it lies in $C_\delta$ by the odd-product clause. These monomials span $P_{\mathrm{even},+}$ by the normal forms of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction]; coefficients in $P_0$ are even multipliers. Closure under sums and $0\in C_\delta$ prove $P_{\mathrm{even},+}=C_\delta$, which gives the required identity for every homogeneous positive even $x$.

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $\delta''$ be a competing operator and transport it to $P'$ by $\phi$. It is zero on $P_0$, since it has degree $-1$. On an odd generator its value is prescribed, and on the divided powers $\gamma_m(T)=T^{[m]}$ of a positive even generator its value is forced to be $v_TT^{[m-1]}$ by the required compatibility. The signed Leibniz rule then forces its value on $aT^{[m]}$ to be the formula in step 2, once its restriction to $A$ is fixed. Induct through the stages of $P'$ and use their union to obtain equality everywhere, using the unique module expressions in [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction]. None of these equations involves $\delta(v_T)$ or requires $\delta^2=0$.
